dedupe_keys.name: global maps of travel time to hospitals emergency hospitals and tertiary hospitals openstreetmap drive time isochrones 2026

description: This dataset maps how far the world's population lives from hospitals of different capability, published with a 2026 preprint by Johan Emilsson. Drive-time isochrones of 15, 30 and 60 minutes were routed on the OpenStreetMap car network from all 217,841 hospitals mapped in OpenStreetMap and dissolved for nested capability tiers: any hospital, hospitals tagged as having an emergency department, and emergency hospitals with a helipad or university-hospital name as a marker of tertiary care. Coverage is weighted with the GHS-POP 2025 population grid and benchmarked against the Weiss et al. 2020 friction-surface travel-time raster. Results: 96.2% of people live within an hour's drive of a hospital, 78.5% of one with a documented emergency department and 40.3% of a tertiary-marked hospital. Outputs include country and global tables, 0.25-degree coverage rasters, dissolved polygons and sensitivity tables, with analysis code and a Docker environment in a GitHub repository under the MIT licence; large files are release assets. Caveats: capability tiers rely on OpenStreetMap tags that are incomplete in many countries, drive times assume free-flow car travel, and the paper is not yet peer reviewed. Simulation uses: estimating populations cut off from emergency care when roads or hospitals fail, prioritising new emergency facilities, and validating accessibility models. Related records: the HeiGIT risk assessment indicators (data-heigit-risk-assessment-indicators-hdx) give district access measures and healthsites.io (data-healthsites-io) maps facilities.
